title: Small, secure images and registries
summary: Pick a base image, run as non-root, then tag and push with versions you can trust.

steps.title: Choosing a base image
body: The base image is usually most of your image's size and almost all of its vulnerabilities.
| base | approx. size | has a shell / package manager | notes |
| `debian:trixie` | 120 MB | yes / apt | familiar, large |
| `debian:trixie-slim` | 75 MB | yes / apt | the usual default |
| `alpine:3.22` | 8 MB | yes / apk | uses **musl** libc, not glibc |
| distroless (`gcr.io/distroless/...`) | 20 MB+ | no / no | only the runtime and its libs |
| .NET **chiseled** (`aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled`) | ~110 MB | no / no | Ubuntu-based distroless for .NET, non-root by default |
| `scratch` | 0 | no / no | empty: for static binaries (Go, Rust) |

Fewer packages means fewer CVEs and nothing for an attacker to use. The cost: no `sh` to `exec` into, so debugging needs other tools (a debug variant, or `docker cp` and logs). Alpine's musl occasionally breaks native libraries compiled for glibc.

steps.prompt: An image moves from `node:22` to `node:22-alpine` and a native npm module now crashes on start with a symbol error. What is the most likely reason?
options: Alpine uses musl libc, and the module's prebuilt binary was compiled against glibc
Alpine images cannot listen on ports
Alpine images run as non-root and cannot load modules
steps.explain: Either rebuild the module for musl (install build tools in the build stage), or use a slim Debian base.

steps.title: Do not run as root
body: By default the process in a container runs as **root** (UID 0). If an attacker breaks out of your app, root in the container is a much better starting point than an unprivileged user, and some escapes need root.
```dockerfile
# Debian/Ubuntu-based
RUN groupadd --system app && useradd --system --gid app app
USER app
# Node official images ship a "node" user
USER node
# .NET 8+ images ship an "app" user and set APP_UID
USER $APP_UID
Consequences to plan for:
- A non-root process cannot bind ports below 1024. That is why .NET 8+ images listen on **8080** by default (`ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080`), not 80.
- Files the app must write need the right owner: `COPY --chown=app:app ...`.

steps.prompt: After upgrading to the .NET 8 base image, `docker run -p 8080:80 api` no longer works, although the app starts fine. Why?
options: The .NET 8+ images run as a non-root user and listen on 8080 by default, so container port 80 has nothing behind it
Port 80 must now be published as `-p 80:80`
The image needs `EXPOSE 80` to start Kestrel
steps.explain: Publish `-p 8080:8080`, or set `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS`. Prefer keeping 8080 so the app can stay non-root.

steps.prompt: Make the final stage of a Debian-based image run as an unprivileged user that owns `/app`.
code: RUN groupadd --system app && useradd --system --gid app app
steps.explain: `--chown` sets the owner as the files are copied, without an extra layer. `chmod 777` would "work" and let anyone write anywhere.

steps.title: Tags, digests and pushing
body: ```text
docker build -t api:1.4.2 .                              build and tag locally
docker tag api:1.4.2 ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4.2              add a name that points at the registry
docker login ghcr.io                                     authenticate once
docker push ghcr.io/acme/api:1.4.2                       upload the layers the registry does not have
A **tag** is a movable label. Teams usually push several for one build: `1.4.2`, `1.4`, the git SHA `sha-3f2a9c1`, and maybe `latest`.
A **digest** (`ghcr.io/acme/api@sha256:9b1c...`) is the hash of the image itself. It can never point at different content, so it is the safest thing to deploy or to pin a base image to.
Only layers the registry lacks are uploaded, which is why a well-cached image pushes in seconds after a small change.

steps.prompt: Arrange the steps to publish version 1.4.2 of the API to GitHub's registry.
steps.explain: Login can happen any time before the push.

steps.prompt: Match each base image to when you would pick it.
pairs: a statically linked Go binary that needs nothing else
a .NET API where you want no shell and non-root by default
a general app that needs apt packages and glibc
tiny utility images where musl is not a problem

steps.title: Lint a Dockerfile
prompt: Write `List<string> Lint(List<string> lines)` that reports these problems in line order (lines are numbered from 1):
1. `FROM` without a tag, or with `:latest` → `line N: pin the base image tag`. A digest (`@sha256:`) counts as pinned. Skip `scratch` and names of earlier stages (`FROM build AS x`).
3. `RUN` containing `apt-get install` but not `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists` → `line N: clean apt lists in the same RUN`
4. `ENV` or `ARG` whose line contains `PASSWORD`, `SECRET` or `TOKEN` (any case) → `line N: secret in ENV or ARG`
Then, if the **final** stage (after the last `FROM`) has no `USER` line, or its last `USER` is `root` or `0`, add `final stage runs as root: add a USER` at the end. Instructions may be in any case.
solution: if (!last.Contains(':') || last.EndsWith(":latest")) warnings.Add($"line {n}: pin the base image tag");
warnings.Add($"line {n}: clean apt lists in the same RUN");
warnings.Add($"line {n}: secret in ENV or ARG");
if (!nonRoot) warnings.Add("final stage runs as root: add a USER");
template: Dojo.Eq("a clean file", new List<string>(), Lint(new List<string> { "FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build", "RUN dotnet publish -o /out", "FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0", "COPY --from=build /out /app", "USER $APP_UID" }));

Dojo.Eq("untagged and latest bases", new List<string> { "line 1: pin the base image tag", "line 2: pin the base image tag", "final stage runs as root: add a USER" }, Lint(new List<string> { "FROM node", "FROM ghcr.io/acme/base:latest" }));

Dojo.Eq("digest, scratch and stage names are fine", new List<string> { "final stage runs as root: add a USER" }, Lint(new List<string> { "FROM golang@sha256:abc AS build", "FROM build AS test", "FROM scratch" }));

Dojo.Eq("ADD, apt and secrets", new List<string> { "line 2: prefer COPY over ADD", "line 3: clean apt lists in the same RUN", "line 5: secret in ENV or ARG", "line 6: secret in ENV or ARG" }, Lint(new List<string> { "FROM debian:bookworm-slim", "ADD app.tar.gz /app", "RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl", "RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y git && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*", "env DB_PASSWORD=hunter2", "ARG npm_token", "USER app" }));

Dojo.Eq("USER only counts in the final stage", new List<string> { "final stage runs as root: add a USER" }, Lint(new List<string> { "FROM node:22-alpine AS build", "USER node", "FROM node:22-alpine" }));
Dojo.Eq("USER root does not count", new List<string> { "final stage runs as root: add a USER" }, Lint(new List<string> { "FROM node:22-alpine", "USER node", "USER root" }));
hints: Reset a `nonRoot` flag on every `FROM`; set it from each `USER` line.
Remember stage names from `FROM x AS name` so a later `FROM name` is not flagged.
For the tag check, look only at the part after the last `/`, so `localhost:5000/api` is not mistaken for tagged.
